newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mutual funds' assets down 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mutual funds' assets down 0.4 pct.

text.p: Israeli mutual funds' assets fell 0.4 percent in September to 12.92 billion shekels from 12.97 billion shekels at the end of August, Meitav Investments and Securities said in a report on Sunday.
The assets declined despite the funds' average positive returns of 2.6 percent in September, mainly because of continued public redemptions from mutual funds, albeit on a lesser scale.
In September redemptions totalled 334 million shekels against 335 million shekels in August.
Most of the redemptions were in funds specialising in shares and bonds.
The positive returns were due to higher stock and bond prices in September, the report said.

Shares were up an average 3.6 percent in September, while bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) gained an average 3.5 percent. Unlinked bonds rose an average 1.5 percent, while Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills increased an average 1.3 percent. Dollar-linked bonds rose an average 2.9 percent in September, the report said.
